title: Sequenced wave promotion with version-contract manifests and auto-rollback playbook
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) control plane upgrades currently rely on manual wave definitions and ad-hoc health checks. That increases human toil during upgrades and leads to uneven safety guarantees across tenants. Goal: Implement a sequenced wave promotion system driven by version-contract manifests and quorum-validated health gates. The system should be operable via Terraform modules, include a dry-run simulation mode, and provide automated rollback when health contracts fail.

Scope:
- Design a version-contract manifest format that encodes compatibility constraints (API contracts, DB migrations, operator version expectations) and required telemetry signals.
- Add Terraform primitives to declare waves, selectors, and rollout policies for private control planes.
- Implement an orchestrator that promotes control plane instances in waves; each wave promotion must validate a quorum of health signals before proceeding.
- Build a dry-run simulator that can be executed as part of a CI preflight to detect potential incompatibilities and estimate promotion timings.
- Define and implement automatic rollback actions tied to contract violations and rate-limited failure budgets.
- Integrate with Console dashboards and alerting for visibility and manual intervention.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the entire control plane reconciliation engine. This work coordinates existing upgrade primitives and augments them with promotion/rollback policy and IaC integration.
acceptance_criteria: Version-contract manifest schema documented and published (Confluence link)
Terraform module (modules/controlplane/rollout) supports wave declarations, selectors, and contract references
Orchestrator service can execute a wave promotion against a staging tenant pool and emit health-evaluation decisions
Promotion halts and triggers rollback when quorum health checks fail according to configured thresholds
Dry-run simulation reproduces promotion plan and flags contract mismatches with actionable diagnostics
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating a two-wave promotion with automatic rollback in CI
tasks: Draft version-contract manifest schema and examples
Prototype terraform module for rollout declarations and selectors
Wire telemetry queries (latency, error-rate, reconciliation lag, API conformance) into gate logic
Add dry-run simulator and CI job that validates manifests against current cluster state
Create console UI surface for observing active promotions and manual aborts
Write e2e test harness and run for three sample tenants
Author runbook for manual recovery and for responding to rollout failures
notes:
Design trade-offs considered: use of quorum-validation vs single-leader gating; opting for quorum to reduce blast radius and enable faster rollback decisions when a statistically significant fraction of tenants show degradation. We chose a manifest-first approach so Terraform can declare and pin expected contracts rather than embedding logic in the orchestrator.

Operational concerns: ensure telemetry queries are performant and cached; avoid promotion blocking on noisy signals by vetting which metrics and aggregation windows are used. Rollback must be idempotent and safe to trigger multiple times.

Open questions:
- How many waves by default? (proposal: 3 waves with exponentially increasing tenant fraction)
- Circuit-breaker cooldown policy and backoff windows for automatic re-promote attempts
- How to represent tenant-scoped overrides in manifests without exploding complexity
